tasks.spec:
You are fixing two prompt defects found by a live smoke run in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. No network, no billed call, no uv: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp`, run `.venv/bin/python`. Do not git commit. YOU MAY EDIT: storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py, tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py, tests/test_recent_cue_reference.py, and existing tests only where a pin truly changes (list each). Never edit data/, bench/frozen/, docs/testing-runbook.md; do not reformat unrelated text. Shared runtime has NO story names.

DEFECT 1: place scoping is defeated by the name-matcher's 'refers'. The place-scoped narrator prompt (item_facts.py `_thing_names`, ~line 540 to 562) keeps a thing if it is in `self._referred_names` ('always keep any thing the player's own command names'). But `_referred_names` is filled from the NAME-MATCHING LLM call, and for a bare command like 'look around' that call lists nearly every thing in its input. Live: while the protagonist sat in the truck outside, the THINGS and PLAYER sections of the narrator prompt still listed drawer, pens, stapler, batteries, Michelle's phone, workstation and chair, and the narrator wrote 'She sees Michelle's phone on the kitchen floor.' FIX: keep a distant thing only when the player's own command LITERALLY names it. Use the engine's own literal test already imported in item_facts.py (`_command_names_thing(command, world.names(entity_id))` from storygame.runtime.seating, which also handles possessives) applied to `self._example_player_input`, and also keep names the engine resolved from the command (storygame.runtime.reference_resolution.resolved_reference_names(self.state, command), already imported in cloudflare.py). Do NOT keep a thing merely because the LLM 'refers' list contains it. The name-matching call itself is unchanged (it still sees everything).
The 'Say who owns a thing the first time you name it: Michelle's phone, Kristin's laptop.' and 'X stores only...' rules in CONSTRAINTS come from cloudflare.py `_owner_rules` (I already scoped it via `_thing_names` when a where-line exists); verify with the test below that after the fix NO house object name appears anywhere in the narrator user prompt for a seated or outside protagonist and a bare 'Look around.'; if `_owner_rules` or any other rule/constraint builder still lists a house object, scope it the same way and report which.
DEFECT 2: the engine resolved 'the gap' to the drawer for matching (recent_cue_referent_text in recent_cue.py, used in cloudflare.py `_evidence_input`) but never told the narrator; live, the narrator's lead-up for 'feel in the gap' still wrote 'the gap between the door and the frame' in 5 of 5 runs. FIX: when `recent_cue_referent_text` returns a non-empty owner name for the turn, render the PLAYER command line for the narrator as '<command> (meaning the <owner name>)' for example 'feel in the gap (meaning the drawer)'. Store the owner on the provider (reset every turn where `last_reveal_selection` is reset) and apply it in item_facts.py `_player_lines` where the command line is built (and nowhere else: matching, reference resolution and the engine's command_text keep the raw command). If no referent resolves, the prompt is byte-identical to today.

TESTS FIRST. In tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py: (a) 1A, protagonist in truck_driver_seat, 'Look around.', with a stubbed name-matching reply whose `refers` lists EVERY thing (simulate the live behavior by stubbing the matching call's response), the narrator prompt contains none of: drawer, pens, stapler, spare batteries, Michelle's phone, workstation, workstation chair, 'kitchen floor'; (b) same at outside_house; (c) 'Open the drawer.' outside still lists the drawer (command names it); (d) a synthetic-story case for (a) and (c). In tests/test_recent_cue_reference.py: (e) after the first turn 'Go in the house.' the narrator prompt for 'Feel in the gap.' ends with the line '- Feel in the gap. (meaning the drawer)' (match the file's existing way of capturing the prompt), while 'Search the kitchen.' and a turn with no referent show the plain command; the pinned negatives stay green.

FINISH: ruff format and ruff check every .py you touched; run the focused suites in the check (the full suite is run once at the very end of the plan, not here); report each existing test changed and why, and print the narrator user prompt's THINGS, PLAYER and CONSTRAINTS sections for case (a).
